register.text: One row per construction project known to the market, with its stage, value, location, taxonomy, parties and a relevance score per vertical.

relevance.text: The grade of the project's type on the relevance matrix, converted to a number: High 8, Medium 5, Low 2, none blank. A few rows carry a hand-adjusted score between the grades, shown to one decimal.

overall.text: The highest of the ten vertical scores.

owner.text: The engineer the ownership cascade assigns the project to, or none. Each project has at most one owner.

pipeline.text: The sum of the values of every project with an owner, in AED million.

bucket.text: Exactly one sales-activity state per project and vertical, chosen by priority: the highest-priority thing that has happened wins.

open.text: Project-and-vertical pairs whose bucket is Enquiry generated or Quote sent.

orders.text: Project-and-vertical pairs whose bucket is Order received with an activity date in 2026.

chase.text: Projects at Tender, or under construction at 5.0 percent or less, with overall relevance 5.0 or more and no vertical in Project closed; the top twenty by value.

door.text: The party through which the owning vertical reaches the project: at specification stage the MEP consultant, else the lead consultant; at buying stage the main contractor, else the MEP contractor, else the lead consultant.

level.text: The highest management level Halvard has a working relationship with at the party: junior, middle or senior management. A known firm Halvard has never worked with has no level, no rating and no owner.

rating.text: A whole number from 1 to 10 recorded by the relationship owner; none where there is no relationship.

workload.text: Synthetic points per engineer: each owned project counts 3 when its bucket on the engineer's vertical is active (quote, enquiry, profile shared, visit, reached out), 1 for an order or a waiting or quiet bucket, 0 when closed. An engineer is over capacity above 320 points.

norel.text: A firm on the register that Halvard has never worked with: its level, rating and owner are all blank. Not the same as a low rating.

value.text: The project value in AED million to one decimal, as recorded on the register.

completion.text: Percent complete, recorded for projects under construction only; most under-construction rows carry 0.0 until a site report arrives.

precisionPolicy: Money is AED million to one decimal at the project level, rounded once; every rollup is a sum of those one-decimal figures, carried in tenths, so tables that show the same figure tie exactly.
Relevance scores are 0.0 to 8.0 to one decimal. Grades convert to 8.0, 5.0 and 2.0; a hand-adjusted score keeps one decimal.
Percentages are one decimal from the underlying sums, never from other percentages.
Counts are whole numbers. Ratings are whole numbers from 1 to 10.
Dates are calendar dates. The register is stated as of the data-as-of date, and nothing published carries a generation timestamp.
assumptions: 3,500 projects, drawn over 80 sector, industry and project-type rows with Urban Construction about three quarters of the register, Industrial about a tenth, and Oil, Gas and Fuels, Transport and Utilities sharing the rest.
Project values follow a wide log-normal in AED million, scaled by project type (a fuel station is small, a metro line is large), capped at AED 60,000.0 million.
Stages weight toward Under Construction (about a third) and Design; four completed bands cover a quarter. Completion percent is recorded for under-construction rows only, and most of those carry 0.0.

Parties: 807 consultants and 676 contractors appear on at least one project, drawn with a heavy tail so a few firms sit on many projects. MEP consultants are recorded on 24.3 percent of rows, a main contractor on 67.3 percent and an MEP contractor on 17.1 percent; the contractor record is fullest at Tender and under construction and thins on the older completed rows.
Every name other than the ten verticals and the 24 engineers is built from invented syllables and checked against a list of terms that must never appear.

Relationship level and rating are drawn per firm, with larger books leaning senior; the relationship owner is the engineer owning most of that firm's projects. 12.3 percent of firms are a synthetic no-relationship cohort with no level, rating or owner.

Workload is a synthetic measure, 3 points per active project on the engineer's own vertical and 1 per order or quiet project, against a capacity of 320 points chosen so a few of the 24 books exceed it.
cascade: Step 1, scope floor: a vertical is eligible for a project only when its score is 4.0 or more.

Step 2, stage gate: Concept and Design projects go to a vertical that sells through consultants; Tender and Under Construction at 5.0 percent or less go to a vertical that sells through contractors; Under Construction beyond that and Completed stay unassigned unless a contractor is already appointed, in which case they go to a vertical that sells through contractors.
Step 3, among eligible verticals that pass the gate the highest score wins; a tie goes to the vertical with fewer projects already assigned, then to the earlier vertical in the published order.
Step 4, within the winning vertical the project goes to the engineer with the lowest current pipeline value, so loads are even but not equal.
Step 5, a project with no eligible vertical, or none that passes the gate, has no owner and is counted in the unassigned figure.
Projects are processed in reference order, so the running counts in steps 3 and 4 are reproducible.
bucketRule: Each project and vertical pair carries exactly one bucket, the highest on this list that applies:
10. Contractor or consultant not yet awarded
Order received counts as an order this year when its activity date falls in the fiscal year.
workloadRule: Each owned project earns the engineer points by its activity bucket on the engineer's own vertical: orders (Order received) 1; active (Quote sent, Enquiry generated, Company profile shared, Visit done, Reached out) 3; waiting or quiet (Waiting or follow up, No response, Contractor or consultant not yet awarded, No update) 1; closed (Project closed) 0.
Workload is the sum of those points. Capacity is 320 points for every engineer; an engineer whose workload exceeds it is over capacity.
Both are synthetic: an illustration of the kind of rule a capacity view needs, never a record of hours worked.
relationshipRule: A firm is known when it sits on at least one project of the register. Halvard holds a relationship with a known firm when a level, a rating and an owner are recorded; the three are always recorded together or not at all.

The no-relationship cohort is drawn per firm: a firm with no project owned by Halvard has a 60 percent chance of no relationship, a firm on three projects or fewer 20 percent, a firm on four to eight 5 percent, and a larger book always has one.
The parties page filters on this state, and the "No relationship yet" figure counts exactly those firms.
